items.meta_title: Run VpnHood! SERVER without root | VpnHood!
items.meta_description: Run VpnHood! SERVER on Linux under your own user account, without root: what works differently, and how to start, stop and update it yourself.
items.title: Run VpnHood! SERVER without root
items.lead: The install command needs root. Without it, you can still run the server on Linux under your own user account: you download it and start it yourself, with the few limits below.
items.lim_cloak: Apps always use Cloak Mode, which costs a little speed and battery, as the server's VPN adapter needs root.
items.lim_port: The server cannot use port [server_port], which networks rarely block: Linux lets only root use ports below 1024.
items.lim_boot: It does not start when the machine starts, or restart by itself if it stops. You start it yourself.
items.lim_updates: It does not update itself. You update it yourself, as shown below.
items.lim_os: It changes none of the operating system settings an installed server sets.
items.req_machine: A machine with a public IP address, running Linux on x64 or arm64. System requirements lists the systems it runs on.
items.req_icu: ICU (libicu), a library the server needs. Nearly every system has it, but only root can install it.
items.req_port: A TCP port above 1023 open, both in the machine's firewall and in your hosting provider's. Only root can change the machine's firewall.
items.step_folder: The server keeps its settings, access keys and logs in a [noroot_storage] folder inside the folder you start it from. So run every command on this page from one folder, here [noroot_dir].
items.caption_download: Download the server for the machine's processor, x64 or arm64
items.caption_start: Start it. It keeps running after you sign out
items.step_settings: The port goes in the server's settings file; for its other settings, see Server configuration. The server's log is in [noroot_log].
items.step_key: Create a key with this command. It works as on an installed server: Create your first access key says where the key is printed and how to limit it.
items.step_key_check: [hostendpoints_label] should show your server's public IP address and the port you set. Then install VpnHood! CLIENT on each device, add the key, and connect.
items.step_update: To update it, stop it, run the download commands again, and start it. Your settings and keys stay in [noroot_storage]. Each new release is listed on GitHub; some fix security issues.
items.step_remove: To remove the server, stop it and delete its folder. That deletes its access keys too, so devices that hold them can no longer connect.
